summary.Top Anchor: BENGAL FINANCE AND INVESTMENT PVT LTD

hero.oneLiner: Vasa Denticity (Dentalkart) positions itself not as an e-commerce store but as "the procurement and knowledge infrastructure that Indian dentistry runs on", scaling volume on automation rather than headcount while rebuilding in-house-brand margin and a self-funded balance sheet.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "We are not building an e-commerce store. We are building the procurement and knowledge infrastructure that Indian dentistry runs on." Stated job is to make anything dental accessible and affordable, keep counterfeit products out of the supply chain, and give a dentist in a Tier-3 town the same assortment, price and speed as one in South Delhi.
- Market framing: "India spends four to five dollars per person per year on dental care against three hundred and fifty in the United States, and most of that market is still served by fragmented local distribution."
- Deck states most of the country's dentists sit outside the metros and are still served by fragmented local distribution; Tier 2/Tier 3 reach is FY27 priority 03 — "Same assortment, same price, same speed, wherever the clinic is."
- Runs a standing accountability slide tracking prior market commitments ("Promises vs Delivered"), including one target it marks REVISED, stating: "Where we change a target, we say so and explain why."
- Listed on NSE Emerge; consolidated results comprise Vasa Denticity together with subsidiaries Waldent Innovations, Smileworks and Dentalkart Distribution UK.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Stated philosophy: get there "by scaling volume on automation rather than on headcount, deepening our in-house brand portfolio so that quality and price are within our own control, and holding a clean, largely self-funded balance sheet."
- Working capital is the disclosed capital-allocation lever: inventory-days target glide 120–150 → 90–120 → under 100 days, with 120–150 set as the FY27 glide path.
- Inventories increased ₹12.67 Cr in the quarter, reflecting continued in-house brand stock build; "Full working-capital disclosure returns with the half-year results."
- "Hold the base. Reinvest selectively in technology without giving back the margin gain." No dividend, buyback or fundraising is mentioned anywhere in the deck.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Guidance revised] The medium-term gross margin target was cut from the previously stated "30–33% over the medium term" to 27%–30%, "on review of achievable mix and FX" — the deck flags this itself as REVISED rather than burying it.
- [M&A withdrawn] "Consistent with the 8 May 2026 disclosure following the mutual withdrawal from the proposed IDS Denmed transaction", no inorganic transaction was entered into, or is contemplated, in FY27.
- [Retention target] 180-day cohort retention targeted above 70% in FY27 against FY26's 68%; deck says it is "too early" as the Q1 FY27 cohort matures only in Q3 FY27.
- [Tone / what they are not doing] "We are not raising guidance on the back of one quarter. We are not calling the margin recovery complete. We are not pursuing inorganic expansion in FY27, and we are not funding growth by adding routine headcount."
- [Earnings call] A live video earnings call is promised, but date and joining details were not disclosed in the deck — to follow via NSE filing.
